To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
human chromosomes and chromosome subsegments can be painted by probes generated from hybrid somatic cells by PCR using primers that recognize interspersed repetitive sequences (Alu and L1).
the combination of PCR with interspersed repetitive sequence primers (IRS-PCR) and chromosomal in situ suppresion (CISS) hybridization allows the generation of probe pools for chromosome painting.
human chromosomes and subregions can be painted in normal human lymphocytes using probe pools generated from hybrid cell DNA by Alu- or LI-PCR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of human chromosome-specific probe pools for use in cytological and molecular cytogenetics.
the application of PCR-based methods for the generation of chromosome-specific probes for the analysis of somatic cell hybrid panels and for the identification of human chromosome aberrations.
the development and application of molecular cytogenetics in human genetics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of PCR generated probes for the identification of human chromosome regions is a very powerful approach.
this is a powerful new approach to chromosome identification and analysis.
this is a new and very promising approach for the generation of chromosome-specific probes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that probe pools generated by PCR from hybrid cell lines can be used for painting of chromosomes in normal human cells.

we have shown that the use of IRS-PCR-generated probe pools is a fast, simple and cost-effective method to obtain chromosome painting probes from hybrid cell lines and thus, a valuable alternative to the conventional approach of generating chromosome specific probes by microcloning.
we have shown that it is possible to use PCR-generated probes for chromosome painting.

it is possible to generate chromosome painting probes by PCR with Alus and L1s.
the combination of PCR and FISH is a powerful tool in the hands of cytogeneticists and molecular geneticists.
